subject: Arcadia HealthTech — sudden P95 spike and elevated 500s on private cluster; tuning + exec coordination
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@arcadia.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: ops+arcadia@arcadia.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ACTION] Private cluster P95 spike + 500 rate increase (started 13:40 PDT)

Hi Aditya,

Sorry to escalate via email but we're seeing a sharp P95 jump and a sustained increase in 5xx responses from our Redwood private cluster (VPC) starting ~13:40 PDT. Latency map attached (csv) and I've pasted representative error snippets in the attachments. Impact: our triage pipeline is timing out for two downstream services and SLA breaches are imminent for our triage tier.

What we see:
- P50 unchanged (~120ms) but P95 moved from ~800ms to ~2.3s
- 5xx rate from 0.2% -> 4.6% over 25 minutes
- Throughput steady but tail latency increases only in inference route /v1/generate (short prompts)

We've already rebooted the three worker nodes and warmed caches; errors persisted after reboot. Can you confirm whether there were any rollout/patches on your side or kernel changes? This is on our Private deployment (account: Arcadia HealthTech). This is impacting our customers, so we need an urgent path to stabilize + a tuning plan.

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Cho, Director of Platform Ops
Arcadia HealthTech

Attachments: arcadia_q2_metrics_snapshot.csv, arcadia_error_snippets.txt

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@arcadia.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Private cluster P95 spike + 500 rate increase (started 13:40 PDT)

Thanks for the data, Samantha — I see the spike in the CSV. I'm escalating to engineering and we'll triage immediately. Quick notes and asks: 

1) No scheduled rollouts/patches from Redwood in that window for your v1/generate model config. We did push a config optimization to a different customer at ~12:50 but not to Arcadia.
2) Can you share a small obfuscated request/trace that reproduces the 5xx? The error snippets hint at OOM in the tokenize path but we need a reproducer.
3) We'll open a Jira (ARC-1345) and propose a short remediation plan:
   - Immediate: Canary on trimmed kernel path + enable conservative batching (reduce max_batch_size) to reduce tail amplification
   - 60–90m: Run a targeted KV-cache priming job and enable prefix caching for high-frequency prompt families
   - 24h: If persists, fallback to model-quant variant (lower mem) and schedule maintenance window for full kernel revert/rollforward

Laura / Rishi — can you two take primary on the canary and kernel diagnostics? Laura, please prepare a small patch we can canary to Arcadia's private pool; Rishi, grab the logs and correlate node-level GPU mem pressure.

Samantha — I'll book a sync in 15 minutes to walk through what we see and I'll share a secure link for logs.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@arcadia.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Private cluster P95 spike + 500 rate increase (started 13:40 PDT)

Looping in Ben for telemetry + canary support. Quick findings from a first-pass on the logs I pulled from Arcadia's control plane:
- A subset of requests with longer prefix tokens show repeated KV cache misses and large decode loops.
- Node-level observation: one worker shows sustained GPU memory fragmentation over 30 mins which correlates to the p95 jump.

Immediate plan I'm pushing now:
1) Push conservative canary (redwood_canary_patch.diff) that forces smaller per-shard batch sizes and reduces prefetch concurrency — this should reduce mem amplification and drop tail.
2) Temporarily enable per-request fallback to the model-quant variant for requests > 1k tokens (policy toggle) — reduces mem footprint.
3) Rishi, please snapshot GPU allocation and capture nvml logs (attach).

Ben — please stand by to run the canary on the 3-node private pool and monitor p95/5xx in real time. I will push the diff to the secure drive link.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@arcadia.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, ops+arcadia@arcadia.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:49:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Private cluster P95 spike + 500 rate increase (started 13:40 PDT)

Appreciate the quick triage. Attached a sanitized trace that reproduces a 500 (gives the request body + response headers). We're green for a canary now — please coordinate start time; our on-call will monitor and can flip routing if anything regresses. Also, our VP of Engineering (mike.lee@arcadia.ai) asked to be looped for exec visibility; looping Mike.

For the 24h plan: we need an estimate of customer impact if we fallback to model-quant variant (latency vs accuracy delta) — our product folks will need that to approve.

Attachments: arcadia_reproducer_trace.json (sanitized)

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@arcadia.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Private cluster P95 spike + 500 rate increase (started 13:40 PDT)

Status update after the canary:

Summary:
- Canary rolled at 15:10 PDT, started with 5% traffic -> 20% -> 100% over 22 minutes.
- Immediate effect: P95 fell from ~2.3s -> ~780ms; 5xx rate dropped to 0.15% within 12 minutes of reaching 20% traffic.
- Root cause (preliminary): a combination of KV cache eviction storms caused by certain high-cardinality prompt families and a less-robust kernel path for the specific model config that led to GPU mem fragmentation.

Next steps and asks:
1) We'll keep the conservative canary active for 24h while we:
   - run a short job to rebuild prefix hot-sets (KV-priming) tonight at 01:00 PDT
   - exercise a targeted GC + allocator defragmentation on the impacted worker (maintenance) tomorrow 03:00 PDT
2) Laura will prepare a formal mitigation playbook for your ops team to run autonomously if this pattern recurs.
3) Product question for Arcadia: are you comfortable with a fallback to model-quant for low-latency SLAs for up to 6% of traffic during peak windows? We estimate 6% quality regressions in edge cases from our internal evals but a 60–70% token cost reduction.

I'll attach the NVML snapshots and the canary diff to the Jira ticket. Marking ARC-1345 as "urgent/mitigated" for now; we'll follow up with a post-mortem.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
